I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then trace the current and inherited evidence before touching the controller. I’ll stay within this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted shelf or neighboring configurations.

I’m using `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because the sampled rollouts include wake keyframe sheets; it requires anchoring those visuals to observations, metrics, and diagnostics before any policy edit. I’ll compare the strongest finite rollout with the most informative failure, then write the diagnosis before changing the candidate.

The scalar evidence separates two mechanisms: the seed and bounded sign-reversed variants remain numerically finite but mostly follow the wake out of the domain, while positive bearing curvature is the only sampled controller with meaningful upstream progress and lateral restraint, yet it saturates both accelerations and explodes the force/moment loads. I’m now checking whether the keyframes support that interpretation and what visible event precedes each termination.

The keyframes confirm the important new result: both conservative radial-phase candidates remain low-load but appear almost passive, drifting downstream/right and downward without ever approaching the wake corridor. By contrast, both angle-only oscillators produce active upstream motion; the bearing-guided one overcorrects into nearly horizontal travel and then folds catastrophically. I’m recording a single isolation hypothesis: keep that demonstrated angle-only propulsion and positive bearing sign, lower the steering bias to recover diagonal descent, and make protection activate only near excessive joint angle/rate so nominal gait energy is not continuously suppressed.

The candidate is now one bounded bearing-only policy, not a sibling set: it preserves the sampled upstream-producing oscillator, reduces the turn bias from 16° to 12°, and adds thresholded state guards plus a high-order acceleration bound. The wake-visual skill’s evidence changes the inherited guidance materially: “phase-energy regulation” is no longer a generic recommendation, because both sampled implementations traded instability for passive downstream exit.

The reusable-guidance provenance check passes. I’m now running the remaining two checks specified by `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml`: the lightweight Julia contract/schema execution and the solver editable-boundary audit. No CFD rollout is being run.

The boundary audit passes after correcting my first invocation’s baseline path. Julia itself is not installed on `PATH`, so the configured execution check cannot run in this environment; I’m checking for any bundled Julia binary and will still run deterministic static schema/bound checks so this environmental absence doesn’t hide a candidate error.
